title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
grouping: Three parts left to right: a small context view (a pale blue square holding a dashed box around one LM layer stacked on one GATED XATTN-DENSE layer, with dotted continuation above and below), two straight lines flaring from that dashed box to a larger dashed panel that expands the pair into its sub-layers, and a grey code panel on the right with the same layer written as Python-like pseudocode.
shapes_depth: Flat square-cornered bars without outlines: frozen language sub-layers (self attention, FFW, LM layer) in medium blue with a snowflake, the new cross-attention and FFW sub-layers in pale lavender. Each sub-layer has a residual skip line rejoining at a small circled-plus above it; small rounded pills labelled 'tanh gating' sit just above the two lavender sub-layers. Attention inputs are tagged K=V=[X] and Q=[Y] beside the bars. Monospace type throughout; the code panel uses syntax colours (pink comments, green docstring).
proposed_highlight: The inserted layers are the lavender ones, the frozen ones blue with snowflakes. The two inputs keep their own colour everywhere: X (vision) in purple and Y (language) in navy, in the side labels, in the K/V/Q tags and at the bottom 'Vision input X' / 'Language input Y'.
lesson: Colour the variable letters themselves (vision X purple, language Y navy) in every input label and K=V=[X] / Q=[Y] tag, so the reader can follow which stream feeds each attention slot without tracing lines.
notes: Pairs the drawing with a code panel that names the same steps, a habit shared with the paper's resampler figure. Venue and year from the PDF footer (NeurIPS 2022).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: A small context square (one LM layer over one GATED XATTN-DENSE in a dashed box) is opened, by two straight lines flaring to the corners, into a larger dashed panel of four stacked sub-layers.

relations.form: dashed box around the layer pair in the left square, two straight lines from its corners to the corners of the larger dashed detail panel to its right
inside the detail panel a bottom-to-top stack: cross attention -> FFW (each with a 'tanh gating' pill) -> frozen self attention -> frozen FFW, each followed by a circled-plus

vision input X enters from below-left and fans into cross attention's K=V tags while language input Y enters below-right as Q=[Y]; in the context square X arrives as a single side arrow into GATED XATTN-DENSE
residual lines rise on the right of each sub-layer into its circled-plus, the same unit repeated four times

channels.colour: training status: blue + snowflake = frozen, lavender = new; the input letters X (purple) and Y (navy) reuse near-identical hues for modality, so purple/blue carry both training status and modality
channels.shape: flat bar = sub-layer, small pill = tanh gate, circled-plus = residual sum
channels.line: solid black arrows for all flow, including residuals; dashed rectangles = zoom boundary and its source
channels.frame: pale-blue square = the LM context; dashed rectangle = the zoomed unit; grey panel = pseudocode

quality.strengths: The zoom is drawn as geometry (straight flaring lines from a small dashed box to a large dashed panel), the frozen/new split is kept from Figure 3 so new sub-layers read at a glance, and the K/V/Q tags name exactly which input each attention bar takes.
quality.weaknesses: No data drawn, only letters X and Y; the gating that defines the method is a tiny pill and a pseudocode comment rather than a drawn element; purple X and lavender layers sit close in hue, mixing modality and training status; the pseudocode panel repeats the diagram's content.

insights.structure: Three parts left to right: a small context square with one LM layer over one GATED XATTN-DENSE inside a dashed box, a larger dashed zoom panel expanding the pair into four sub-layers, and a grey pseudocode panel.
insights.data: Inputs are only letters X (purple, vision) and Y (navy, language) with K=V=[X], Q=[Y] tags beside each attention bar; no data images.
insights.emphasis: Frozen sub-layers are blue with snowflakes, new ones lavender with small 'tanh gating' pills above, and the code panel spells out alpha initialised at 0 in coloured comments.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top through stacked bars, each with a residual line rising on the right into a circled-plus; two straight lines flare from the small dashed box to the zoom panel's corners.

arrangement.units: context panel (pale-blue square with dashed selection), dashed zoom panel, grey code panel, side by side
arrangement.inputs_as: letters X and Y labelled 'Vision input' and 'Language input' below the zoom panel
arrangement.shared: same colour coding frozen/new as fig3
